subject: general
question: The Sone river belongs to which river system?
solution:
The correct answer is** __Ganga.__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Son River**, often written **Sone**, is the **main Ganges (Ganga) River tributary **in the **state of Madhya Pradesh** in **central India.**
 
• After passing **Manpur to the north**, it bends to the **northeast**.
 
• The river travels **487 miles **(784 km) across the **Kaimur Range** before joining the** Ganges above Patna.**
 
• Central India is home to the Son River a perennial river.
 
• It starts near Amarkantak Hill in the Chhattisgarh district of Gaurela-Pendra-Marwahi, and eventually, it joins the Ganges River close to Patna, Bihar.
 
• After the Yamuna River, the Sone River is the Ganges' second-largest tributary in the South.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mahanadi

 
 
• ​In **East Central India**, the **Mahanadi River** is a significant river. It is the world's longest earthen dam. It has a length of 900 miles overall and drains an area of around 132,100 square kilometres.
 
• The **Hirakud Dam**, the first significant multifunctional river valley project following India's independence in 1947, is another reason for the fame of **Mahanadi**.
 
 
 
• **Narmada**
 
 
• The **Narmada River**, also known as the **Reva** and formerly as **Narbada or Nerbudda in English**, is the fifth-longest river in India and the longest west-flowing river altogether. It is also the state of **Madhya Pradesh's greatest flowing river.**
 
• This river traverses the **Indian states of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh**. Due to its enormous contribution to the two states in numerous ways, it is also known as the **"Lifeline of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat."**
 
 
 
• **Godavari**
 
 
• After the **Ganga**, the **Godavari** is the second-longest river in India. It empties into the third-largest basin, which makes up 10% of India's entire land area.
 
• **Trimbakeshwar,** in **Nashik, Maharashtra**, is where it originates. It drains the states of Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha as it travels 1,465 kilometres to the east. ​
